problem: The statement "Confusing variance Var(X) with standard deviation √Var(X) will double the error magnitude" is incorrect. Standard deviation is the square root of variance, not twice the variance.
fix: Replace the sentence with: "Confusing variance Var(X) with standard deviation √Var(X) changes the scale of the error; standard deviation is the square root of variance, not a multiple of it."

problem: The description "We write a column vector as v = [v₁, v₂, …, vₙ]ᵀ" may confuse readers because the transpose symbol on a row‑vector notation is unusual for beginners.
fix: Clarify: "A column vector can be written as a vertical list, e.g. v = \begin{bmatrix}v₁\\v₂\\…\\vₙ\end{bmatrix}. It is also common to write a row vector and add a transpose symbol: v = [v₁, v₂, …, vₙ]ᵀ."

problem: The arrow "y = (w·x) + b → y = w·(x + b)" suggests a correct transformation, but the intention is to show a common mistake.
fix: Rephrase to: "A common mistake is to add the bias before the dot product, writing y = w·(x + b) instead of y = (w·x) + b."
